headline: South & Southeast Asia: US warns Middle East conflict could 'escalate rapidly', urges citizens to reconsider travel
script:
Good morning. Here is your global conflict briefing. The most significant development in the last day comes from the south & southeast asia: US warns Middle East conflict could 'escalate rapidly', urges citizens to reconsider travel, reported by Dawn (Pakistan) 2 hours ago. Full details follow.

Turning to the South & Southeast Asia.
From Dawn (Pakistan), 2 hours ago: US warns Middle East conflict could 'escalate rapidly', urges citizens to reconsider travel.
From Dawn (Pakistan), 21 hours ago: Houthis say targeted 'sensitive sites' in Riyadh, Aramco facilities in Yanbu.
From Dawn (Pakistan), 11 hours ago: Turkiye says it could help meet Saudi Arabia’s military needs.
From Dawn (Pakistan), one day ago: Kohat Police Lines attack: 8 terrorists killed as overnight clearance operation concludes.

Turning to the Asia-Pacific / East Asia.
From South China Morning Post - China, 9 hours ago: Ukraine pummels Moscow with drones on last day of Russian election.
From South China Morning Post - China, 21 hours ago: Houthis claim attacks on Saudi capital, after flames seen near Riyadh airport.
From South China Morning Post - China, 5 hours ago: North Korea fires 2 missiles in 3 hours amid tensions over US drills.
From South China Morning Post - China, 13 hours ago: Some Western politicians stoking Nato-Russia clash as Ukraine war strategy falters: Fico.

Turning to the Russia's Conflicts.
From Ukrainska Pravda, 8 hours ago: Moscow region attacked with multiple weapons, including Flamingo and Pelican, Zelenskyy says – video.
From Ukrainska Pravda, one hour ago: Russian UAVs cause fire in warehouses and damage businesses in Kyiv Oblast – video.
From Ukrainska Pravda, 2 hours ago: Ukraine's 3rd Army Corps deploys air-dropped kamikaze UGV for the first time during offensive in Donetsk Oblast.
From Ukrainska Pravda, 6 hours ago: Ukraine's General Staff details strike on Moscow Oil Refinery, reports hits on Buk-M3 and Nebo-U.

Turning to the Middle East.
From Jerusalem Post, 2 hours ago: Iran claims US preparing to resume attacks, threatens bases, supporting regional countries.
From Jerusalem Post, 2 hours ago: 'No terrorist is immune,' Netanyahu says as IDF chief orders reinforcements to join manhunt.
From Al Jazeera - Middle East, 3 hours ago: Moscow attacked by more than 1,000 Ukrainian drones.
From Jerusalem Post, just now: IDF prepares West Bank mass-arrest operation, demolition of Neveh Tzuf terrorist’s home - report.

Turning to the Korean Peninsula.
From Yonhap News Agency, 8 hours ago: (2nd LD) N. Korea fires 1 short-range ballistic missile toward East Sea: S. Korean military.
From Yonhap News Agency, 8 hours ago: (LEAD) N. Korea fires 1 short-range ballistic missile toward East Sea: S. Korean military.
From NK News, 10 hours ago: North Korea launches suspected ballistic missiles toward East Sea: JCS.
From Yonhap News Agency, 5 hours ago: (4th LD) N. Korea fires 2 short-range ballistic missiles hours apart ahead of Trump-Xi summit.

Turning to the Europe (non-Russia).
From Politico Europe, 7 hours ago: Massive Ukrainian drone attack hits Moscow on last day of Russian elections.
From Politico Europe, one day ago: France’s National Rally criticizes Russia in rare rebuke.

Turning to the United States.
From Military Times, 2 days ago: Soldier identified following rollover crash at Fort Hood.
From Military Times, 2 days ago: Army’s H2F program linked to faster injury recovery among soldiers, study finds.
From Military Times, 2 days ago: Army to promote NCOs who complete drill sergeant, recruiting schools.

Turning to the Africa.
From Africanews, 4 hours ago: Gaza children return to school after years of war and displacement.
From Africanews, 6 hours ago: Uganda suspends military cooperation with Turkey amid political tensions.
From Africanews, 7 hours ago: Congo launches Ebola vaccination campaign for frontline workers.
From Africanews, 9 hours ago: Nigeria appoints panel to probe deaths of 37 miners in holding cell.

Turning to the The Americas.
From Buenos Aires Herald, 3 hours ago: Twenty years without Jorge Julio López, the man who disappeared twice.

This briefing is compiled automatically from regional news feeds and has not been cross-referenced by an editor. Treat single-source claims as unconfirmed. I will be back tomorrow morning.
